| Meeting | Session B leaves you with |
|:---|:---|
| **1** &nbsp;Intro and ideas | Candidate questions of your own, each labelled with an archetype and run through the filter |
| **2** &nbsp;Causal language | Your team's ground rules, and a diagnosed causal graph |
| **3** &nbsp;Models and uncertainty | The overclaim your own project is most at risk of making |
| **4** &nbsp;How inference fails | The one threat your design will have to survive |
| **5** &nbsp;Controls and matching | Which back doors you can close, and with what data |
| **6** &nbsp;Research designs I | Whether an experiment, instrument or discontinuity is open to you |
| **7** &nbsp;Research designs II | Your design defended in public, plus the attack that landed — the identification section and the limitation |
| **8** &nbsp;Writing | Your problem statement, as an outline somebody outside your team could follow |
| **9** &nbsp;Oral and visual | Your project's key figure, and a pitch that survived the room |
| **10** &nbsp;Measurement and data | Your key variable, operationalised — and if you must collect it, the instrument and the sample size it needs |
| **11** &nbsp;Getting the data | Your data source, access route, timeline and plan B |
| **12** &nbsp;Using data | Your own data, interrogated, and what is wrong with it |
| **13** &nbsp;Midterm and workshop | Your outline, marked up by somebody outside your team |
